chunks: Then a man came running from the farthest part of the city. He said, 'O my people, follow the messengers.'
ai.seo_question: Who is the man that came running from the city in Surah Yaseen?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often associated with Abu Jahl or a specific companion who emerged from the periphery to validate the messengers, emphasizing the individual's agency in confronting communal stagnation. The urgency of his running (yas'a) symbolizes the active, dynamic nature of da'wah, contrasting with the complacency of the elite who remained in their palaces. This narrative underscores the Shia principle that truth can be championed by a single righteous individual against the majority's inertia.
